scope: Pinned PCSX2 source explains VIF behavior relevant to interpreting the game packet; it does not establish this game packet state or exact hardware execution.

bounded_facts.claim: The pinned V4 unpack path consults MODE; mode 1 adds MaskRow to source data and mode 2 adds MaskRow and updates it. Thus UNPACK destination plus VU load address alone does not establish literal payload values.
Pinned PCSX2 VIF1 execMicro copies TOPS into TOP, then flips DBF and selects the next TOPS from BASE or BASE+OFFSET.
The game packet has proven MODE=0, contiguous STCYCL and known TOP at MSCAL 0x5cc.

claims: The pinned PCSX2 unmasked V4 unpack path still consults MODE: mode1 adds MaskRow to data and mode2 adds MaskRow and updates it, so matching UNPACK destination and VU load address alone does not prove literal payload value identity.
In the pinned PCSX2 VIF1 execMicro path, TOP is assigned from TOPS before TOPS is updated according to DBF, BASE and OFFSET.
The traced game packet has proven mode0, contiguous STCYCL state and known TOP at MSCAL0x5cc.

evidence.text: Existing static trace of FUN00128ca0 identifies UNPACK0x6c080000 dest0 NUM8 followed by eight qwords and MSCAL0x5cc. Packet preamble/helper traffic, STCYCL/STMOD/ROW and preceding TOPS state have not been fully reconstructed. No original game execution occurred. Selected addresses alone are evidence of compatible layouts, not state proof.

exact_jev_receipt_reference.disposition: Retain the TOP-latch review and unsupported/contradicted game-state result. The MODE result narrows packet-to-register interpretation. No Jev retry.

limitations: PCSX2 is an implementation reference, not direct hardware observation.
The cited TOP sequencing claim is VIF1-specific; this bundle does not establish which VIF instance or pre-existing mode/cycle/row/TOPS state governs FUN_00128ca0.
No exact TOP value at MSCAL 0x5cc is derived.
The V4-32-to-VF01..08 relation is conditional on compatible state and is not asserted as byte-for-byte payload identity.
